subject: Climate & Environment
title: How Tornadoes Form
description: A short lesson to help you apply How Tornadoes Form.

hook.text: Warm, humid air meets cold, dry air. The atmosphere becomes unstable — and starts to rotate.

buildup.text: Supercell thunderstorms create a rotating updraft called a mesocyclone high in the clouds.

discovery.text: When that rotation tightens and touches the ground, a tornado is born.

twist.text: Most tornadoes last under 10 minutes. But in those minutes, they can erase entire neighborhoods.

climax.text: The US averages about 1,200 tornadoes per year — more than any other country.

punchline.text: A tornado is born from a collision of air masses — and dies just as suddenly.

quiz.question: What type of thunderstorm most commonly produces tornadoes?

details.summary: Tornadoes form when rotating updrafts within severe thunderstorms called supercells tilt vertically, stretching a column of spinning air from cloud to ground. The most violent tornadoes produce winds exceeding 300 km/h and can destroy structures in seconds.
details.whyItMatters: Tornadoes are the most violent atmospheric phenomenon. Understanding their formation is key to improving warning times, which currently average only 13 minutes.
takeaways: Supercell thunderstorms produce the most violent tornadoes
Wind shear creates horizontal rotation that updrafts tilt vertical
Average US tornado warning lead time is roughly 13 minutes

faq.question: Can tornadoes be predicted more than minutes in advance?
faq.answer: Meteorologists can identify tornado-favorable conditions hours ahead, but predicting exactly where and when a tornado will touch down remains impossible beyond roughly 15 to 20 minutes. Research into dual-polarization radar aims to improve lead times.

faq.question: Why are US tornadoes the most destructive in the world?
faq.answer: The US Great Plains uniquely combine warm Gulf moisture, cold dry air from Canada, and strong jet-stream wind shear. This atmospheric collision zone produces more violent tornadoes than any other region on Earth.
